article_title: Preservice mathematics teachers’ noticing in AI-based simulations: transitions among attending, interpreting, and shaping
citation: Selen Galiç, Mathias Tejera, Sebastián Parodi, Markus Hohenwarter, Zsolt Lavicza. (2026). Preservice mathematics teachers' noticing in AI-based simulations: transitions among attending, interpreting, and shaping. ZDM – Mathematics Education. https://doi.org/10.1007/s11858-026-01805-4
title: Teacher Noticing of Rationality Framework (TNRF)
description: The TNRF builds on van Es and Sherin's expanded noticing framework of attending, interpreting, and shaping, and "extends van Es and Sherin's (2021) framework by specifying the object of noticing more precisely as students' mathematical thinking". It operationalises students' thinking through Habermas's theory of rationality as observable behaviours: justifying statements, selecting and using appropriate tools, and communicating with appropriate terminology and representations. Attending targets manifestations of rational behaviour rather than surface correctness; interpreting evaluates the quality of participation in mathematical practices; shaping structures conditions under which rational behaviour becomes visible.
requirements: Requires teachers' professional knowledge and an inquiry stance to interpret behaviours through the rationality lens rather than simple correctness judgments
constraints: The article applies the framework specifically to the equal-sign context, with coding adapted to the construct map of the equal sign (Matthews et al., 2012)
target_learning_goals: Noticing students' mathematical thinking in the context of the equal sign as equivalence
examples: The study used the TNRF to inform a deductive coding scheme with subcodes under each noticing dimension, applied to reflection papers and chat interactions
key_sources: Selen Galiç, Mathias Tejera, Sebastián Parodi, Markus Hohenwarter, Zsolt Lavicza. (2026). Preservice mathematics teachers' noticing in AI-based simulations: transitions among attending, interpreting, and shaping. ZDM – Mathematics Education. https://doi.org/10.1007/s11858-026-01805-4

article_title: Evaluation of video review tools for assessing non-technical skills in emergency department resuscitation teams: a systematic review.
citation: Alexander Emily G, Denny Fraser, Gordon Malcom WG, McKiernan Cieran, Lowe David J. (2023). Evaluation of video review tools for assessing non-technical skills in emergency department resuscitation teams: a systematic review. BMC Emergency Medicine. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12873-023-00895-7
title: Use T-NOTECHS as the tool of choice for assessing non-technical skills of ED resuscitation teams via video review
description: The review recommends T-NOTECHS for video-based assessment of NTS in ED resuscitation teams because it is validated, most studied, and balances usability, reliability and validity. It states that "when assessing NTS more holistically, T-NOTECHS demonstrates usability, reliability and validity". T-NOTECHS splits NTS into 5 categories on a 5-point Likert scale and provides score anchors to guide users.
requirements: Video recording of real-life resuscitations in the ED; reviewers can pause or rewind video for more accurate assessment
constraints: The conclusion that T-NOTECHS is the best tool is suggested but not proven fully due to small sample sizes; reliability varies across studies (ICC 0.48–0.94)
target_learning_goals: non-technical skills including leadership, communication, situational awareness, decision making and teamwork
examples: Six of the nine included studies used T-NOTECHS; the review recommends multi-centre studies with larger sample sizes to establish its utility, and suggests TTCA-24 where communication is identified as a weakness
key_sources: Alexander Emily G, Denny Fraser, Gordon Malcom WG, McKiernan Cieran, Lowe David J. (2023). Evaluation of video review tools for assessing non-technical skills in emergency department resuscitation teams: a systematic review. BMC Emergency Medicine. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12873-023-00895-7
